references.description: Denormalized flat join of entity + security.  One row per security — covers the company universe (CIK + primary identifiers + sector + ticker) — plus one row with NULL security_id / symbol for every reporting company that has no security (e.g. a wholly-owned subsidiary that files only because it issues public debt, or a delisted registrant).  Filter symbol IS NOT NULL for listed securities only.  For ANY membership question (current or historical, SP500 or Russell), JOIN with index_membership on cik = cik.  The join column has the same name on both sides — this view does NOT carry index-membership flags because they're inherently snapshot-only and single-index, both of which are footguns the index_membership table avoids by design.

status.description: ACTIVE when the registrant has a ticker in SEC's company_tickers.json on the day the pipeline read that file, else INACTIVE.  This is a statement about the TICKER FILE, not about whether the company still files with the SEC: use `listed today` semantics for it (see `is_public` for the classified view) and `is_active` (on this table `is_entity_active`) for `still alive`.  The two legitimately disagree: a non-traded REIT or a debt-only registrant files every quarter but has no ticker (INACTIVE + is_active TRUE); a company whose ticker lingers in the file after it stopped filing is ACTIVE + is_active FALSE.  Pipeline source: SecProcessor.process_submissions_data (`ACTIVE` iff the CIK is in the ticker map).

is_active.description: The SECURITY's ticker spell is open (security.valid_to IS NULL); NULL on a company with no security.  Says nothing about the registrant: for `still alive` use `is_entity_active`.

is_primary_ticker.description: Propagated from security.is_primary_ticker.  TRUE for the entity's primary listing.  Multi-share-class issuers (BRK-A/BRK-B, GOOG/GOOGL) emit multiple rows here; default consumer queries (and the MCP universe dedup) filter is_primary_ticker=TRUE for one row per CIK.

is_public.description: Propagated from entity.is_public: the registrant is exchange-listed TODAY.  NULL = never classified, not FALSE.  Not the same as `is_active` on this table, which describes the SECURITY's ticker spell.

is_entity_active.description: Propagated from entity.is_active (the entity_status activity spell, else latest filing within DORMANCY_DAYS = 400): the registrant still files with the SEC.  Use it for `still alive`; `status` only says whether the CIK is on SEC's ticker file today, and the two can disagree in both directions (non-traded REIT: status INACTIVE, is_entity_active TRUE).  NULL = never classified.  Not the same as `is_active` on this table, which describes the SECURITY's ticker spell.

succeeded_by_cik.description: Propagated from entity.succeeded_by_cik: the DECLARED corporate-succession link, NULL for almost every row. When present, the registrant on THIS row was reorganised into the CIK named here — a curated, evidence-gated fact (configs/security_successions.csv in data-pipeline), never a ticker-recycling coincidence. A ticker resolver should follow this link instead of guessing succession from which CIK holds more facts.

entity.description: Legal structure and profile of reporting companies.

sic_description.description: Full SEC SIC industry label (e.g. 'Electronic Computers').  Companion to ``sic_code`` — use this on responses where a human-readable string is more useful than the raw 4-digit code.

status.description: ACTIVE when the registrant has a ticker in SEC's company_tickers.json on the day the pipeline read that file, else INACTIVE.  This is a statement about the TICKER FILE, not about whether the company still files with the SEC: use `listed today` semantics for it (see `is_public` for the classified view) and `is_active` (references: `is_entity_active`) for `still alive`.  The two legitimately disagree: a non-traded REIT or a debt-only registrant files every quarter but has no ticker (INACTIVE + is_active TRUE); a company whose ticker lingers in the file after it stopped filing is ACTIVE + is_active FALSE.  Pipeline source: SecProcessor.process_submissions_data (`ACTIVE` iff the CIK is in the ticker map).

state_of_incorporation_description.description: Full SEC label for the state-of-incorporation code (e.g. 'Delaware').

mailing_address.description: Mailing address (separate from HQ) — registered agent / correspondence target.  Often differs from business_address for foreign issuers and trusts.

flags.description: SEC-flagged status string (e.g. 'Shell', 'Delinquent'). NULL for clean issuers.

has_insider_transactions.description: SEC declares Form 4/5 activity exists for this issuer.

is_insider_owner.description: SEC declares this CIK itself owns insider holdings.

is_public.description: TRUE when the registrant's CURRENT listing spell is 'public' (exchange-listed); FALSE for non_traded / unregistered; NULL when no evidence classifies it.  Derived from the entity_status replay classifier (Form 25 / 15, 8-K items, insider / 13D-G / price evidence).

is_active.description: TRUE when the registrant still files with the SEC: its CURRENT entity_status activity spell is 'active'; FALSE when inactive (deregistered, acquired, dormant); with no spell, TRUE iff its latest filing is within DORMANCY_DAYS (400) of today; NULL when it was never classified and has no filing.  Independent of `status`, which only says whether the CIK is on SEC's ticker file: a delisted-but-still-filing company is status INACTIVE + is_active TRUE, a ticker that outlived the company is status ACTIVE + is_active FALSE.  Use this column for `still alive / still reporting`, `status` or `is_public` for `listed today`.

former_names.description: SEC ``formerNames[]`` history — JSON array of ``{name, from, to}`` objects.  Useful for ticker-history queries and merger lineage (e.g. tracing FB → META, GOOG → GOOGL share splits, or a former subsidiary's prior name).  Empty array when the issuer has never renamed.

last_seen_at.description: Pipeline bookkeeping, not a company fact: the date of the last pipeline run that refreshed this row from SEC's submissions file.  After a full run every company carries the same date; it says nothing about when the company last filed — use MAX(filing.filing_date) for that, and is_active for "still reporting".

succeeded_by_cik.description: The DECLARED corporate-succession link: NULL for the overwhelmingly common case, else the CIK of the registrant this one was reorganised into (a redomestication, holdco inversion, or similar SEC-issued-a-new-CIK event). Written by SecuritySuccessionService from ``configs/security_successions.csv``, which only accepts a pair whose successor RESTATES the predecessor's numbers (>= 25 identical fact tuples). Never a ticker-recycling coincidence (DEC, AMR, ARC), never inferred from which CIK holds more facts — that proxy is exactly what this column replaces for consumers. Propagated onto ``references`` at export.

security.description: Ticker symbols and tradeable instrument metadata (SCD Type 2 with date ranges).

is_primary_ticker.description: True for the ticker SEC's company_tickers.json marks as the entity's primary listing.  Multi-share-class issuers (BRK-A/BRK-B, GOOG/GOOGL) emit multiple is_active=TRUE rows; default consumer queries filter is_primary_ticker=TRUE for one row per CIK.

filing.description: Metadata for all SEC filings processed.

superseded_by.description: Accession-id of the filing that supersedes this one in the amendment chain (NULL when this is the latest version).  Populated post-ingest by ``services/filings/amendment_linker.py``.

size.description: Filing size in bytes (per SEC submissions feed).

is_xbrl.description: SEC-declared: filing carries an XBRL exhibit.

is_xbrl_numeric.description: Distinct from is_xbrl/is_inline_xbrl — TRUE when the XBRL exhibit carries machine-readable numeric facts (the source of every fact-table row).

primary_document.description: Filename of the lead document in the filing package.

primary_doc_description.description: SEC-provided label describing the primary document.

core_type.description: Base form_type stripped of the ``/A`` amendment suffix (e.g. ``10-K/A`` → ``10-K``).  Use this for form-family filtering when you don't care whether a filing is the original or an amendment.

film_number.description: SEC EDGAR microfiche / film number assigned at acceptance.

act.description: Securities-Act designator: ``33`` (1933 Act), ``34`` (1934 Act), or empty.  Helps distinguish registration-statement vs. exchange-act filings.

is_audited.description: Filing is an annual (audited) report — TRUE for 10-K / 20-F / 40-F and their amendments, FALSE for 10-Q / 8-K / etc.

fact.description: Standardized financial data points (US-GAAP XBRL mapped to canonical standard_concept labels).

fact_id.description: Deterministic identity hash: SHA-256(entity_id|accession_id|concept|period_end|unit). Matches the Postgres unique constraint idx_fact_unique_constraint. Computed at export time by run_exports.py — not stored in the database.

concept.description: The RAW XBRL tag as filed (bare local name, e.g. 'Revenues').  Look it up in ``taxonomy_guide.standard_concept``.

standard_concept.description: Valuein's curated canonical concept (e.g. 'Revenue'; 'Other' when unmapped or not CPA-reviewed).  Look it up in the ``standard_concept`` table.

priority.description: Primary-row flag, computed at export: within each filing (accession_id), 1 on the row of the raw tag elected for this (entity_id, standard_concept, period_end, unit, duration) fact, 0 on sibling tags that map to the same standard concept.  Every filing therefore has exactly one priority-1 row per fact.  Election order: source tier (XBRL first), mapping accuracy (exact tag match first), a tag whose every value is 0 loses to one that is not, CONCEPT_PRECEDENCE rank, tag name.  Filter ``priority = 1`` for one row per fact per filing.

value.description: Raw as-reported value string, before numeric parsing.  Holds text for non-numeric facts (e.g. dei cover-page strings); for numeric facts prefer ``numeric_value``.

numeric_value.description: The value as reported in this specific filing (accession_id).

fiscal_year.description: Fiscal year the fact's ``period_end`` belongs to, derived from the entity's fiscal-year end (not SEC's cover-page fy): a comparative in a later 10-K keeps its own period's year.  Group by ``period_end`` when exactness matters.

accuracy_score.description: Legacy 0-1 standardization-match score stamped by the in-memory resolver at ingest.  Superseded for consumer filtering by ``confidence_score`` (the composite quality score); kept for traceability of the concept mapping.

confidence_score.description: Per-fact confidence in [0, 1] — a PENALTY FROM EVIDENCE, not an opinion. Every fact starts at 1.0 and is docked only for something we can point at. Formula (v2): 1.0 - 0.40 * min(identity_violation_count / 3, 1) - 0.20 * min(restatement_count / 5, 1) - 0.05 * (NOT is_audited). Every input ships in this same table, so you can RECOMPUTE this number and check us — that is deliberate. Read it as: >= 0.95 we hold no evidence against this fact (the normal case, ~99.9% of rows, across all years); ~0.80 a later filing revised it (see the restatement diff on /radar); < 0.60 an accounting identity FAILED on its filing. NB there is deliberately no age term: an older filing is not less trustworthy, it is more settled, and a score that decays with age would turn `>= 0.95` into a recency filter on a point-in-time, survivorship-free dataset.

reliability_code.description: NOMINAL reliability bucket (1-4) for Bloomberg PR / Refinitiv vendor parity: 1=preliminary (identity errors present), 2=announced (clean, unaudited), 3=audited (audited + clean), 4=restated (audited + clean + multiple versions on file). ⚠️ NOT AN ORDINAL — 4 ('restated') is not 'better' than 3 ('audited, clean'), despite being the larger number, so `WHERE reliability_code >= 3` silently INCLUDES restated facts. To rank by quality, order by confidence_score; use this column only for equality tests against a specific bucket.

identity_violation_count.description: Number of error-severity accounting identities that fired against this fact's filing.  Sourced from qa_violation.

restatement_count.description: Number of times this fact has been re-reported across accessions. Grain is (entity, RAW XBRL concept, period_start, period_end, unit) — sourced from fact_lineage_summary.version_count - 1. Zero = never restated; > 0 = restated N times. NB the grain is the raw filer tag and the reporting WINDOW, never our standardized concept (a mapping collapses ~12k tags onto ~283 names, so grouping on it diffs values that were never comparable) and never fiscal_period (a derived LABEL, sometimes missing and sometimes wrong — putting it in a grain splits one fact into several). Both mistakes INVENT restatements.

is_estimated.description: TRUE when part of the published value was INFERRED rather than read from the source. In practice this means a monetary SCALE: the EX-27 Financial Data Schedules that carry our 1994-2001 history omit their <MULTIPLIER> tag on ~27% of schedules, and a missing scale is invisible to every accounting identity because every line is wrong by the same factor. Where the scale was pinned by an anchor outside the monetary block (the filer's own declaration on another schedule, or the EPS-implied share count) the fact ships with this flag set and a confidence_score deduction; where it could not be pinned, the monetary fact was not published at all. On XBRL-sourced facts it is FALSE except for a share count or EPS the pipeline's magnitude guard touched: a filer's own units slip (e.g. 59,711,000,000 diluted shares typed for 59,711,000) is either corrected by an exact power of 1000 against independent evidence (EPS = net income / weighted shares, another filing's value for the same period, the company's own share-count series; `numeric_value` is the corrected figure and `value` keeps the filer's string) or, when nothing corroborates a fix, left as filed and flagged. Both carry TRUE and the same confidence_score deduction.

data_quality.description: How this number was obtained. 'standard' = read from an XBRL exhibit the filer tagged (2009-present; the overwhelming majority of the table). 'ex27_fds' = parsed from an SEC EX-27 Financial Data Schedule, the tagged machine-readable summary that Reg S-T Rules 401/402 required on every 10-K and 10-Q from 1994-09-01 until the rescission effective 2001-01-01 — still the filer's own tagged number, one layer of our parsing away. 'html_derived' = extracted by us from the filing's rendered financial statements (2001-2008, where no machine-readable exhibit exists). 'sgml_derived' = extracted by us from the fixed-width SGML statements of a pre-2003 filing, sliced at the filer's own column offsets. 'human_verified' = a value a named reviewer read off the filing by hand and recorded with the page/line evidence and a sec.gov link (the evidence is in `label`; the raw tag is 'human:<concept>'); it replaces the parser lanes' value for that series, is never estimated, ships at confidence 1.0, and is still outranked by an XBRL value for the same series. Filter on this column to restrict a backtest to XBRL-era facts; the confidence_score already carries a deduction for the other two, and the raw source tag is preserved in `concept` (an 'fds5:'-style prefix) so any recovered value traces to a specific line of a specific exhibit. 'period_after_filing' = a statement or cover-page fact (revenue, net income, assets, equity, cash, shares outstanding, public float, ...) whose period ends more than a day AFTER the filing was accepted: a date the filer mistyped (cover shares dated a year ahead). The value is kept, never dropped; `data_quality = 'standard'` excludes it. Forward-looking concepts (future minimum rents, amortisation schedules, declared dividends) end after the filing by nature and are not flagged.

accounting_standard.description: Reporting taxonomy of the source filing — 'US-GAAP' or 'IFRS'.  Derived from the XBRL taxonomy; defaults 'US-GAAP' for 10-K/10-Q/8-K and is usually 'IFRS' for 20-F / 40-F foreign issuers.

reporting_currency.description: ISO-4217 currency code when the unit is a monetary currency (e.g. 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY').  NULL for non-monetary facts (shares, ratios, days, etc.).

value_current.description: Bloomberg Option-C: the latest-known value for this (entity_id, standard_concept, period_end, unit) — i.e., the value any analyst watching the tape TODAY would see. Computed at export time via DuckDB window functions.

value_as_filed.description: Bloomberg Option-C: the originally-reported value (first-ever accepted_at in the partition).

first_filed_at.description: Timestamp of first disclosure (min accepted_at in the partition).

restated.description: TRUE if any version of this fact in the partition differs from the others — signals that a later filing restated this number.  WARNING: this signal is computed against the GLOBAL state of the warehouse, NOT PIT — a query with as_of_date in the past may still see TRUE for a fact whose restatement happened AFTER the cutoff.  Treat as informational; for PIT reasoning, the MCP server exposes this as ``lineage.restated_in_warehouse`` so consumers know the field is not PIT-safe (audit CC-004).

filing_registrant.description: Every registrant of an SEC accession.  ``filing`` has ONE row per ``accession_id``, owned by the first registrant, so a combined (co-registrant) filing appears under only one CIK there; ``fact.entity_id`` still names each registrant.  Join this table to ``filing`` on ``accession_id`` to list a company's filings including the combined ones: ``SELECT f.* FROM filing f JOIN filing_registrant r ON r.accession_id = f.accession_id WHERE r.entity_id = :cik``.  A registrant that filed no numeric fact under its own CIK may be absent.

entity_id.description: One registrant of the accession (10-digit CIK).

index_membership.description:
Index constituents keyed on ``cik``.  Always JOIN ``references.cik = index_membership.cik`` to attach company metadata (name, sector, ticker).  Filter by ``index_name`` for the index, by ``effective_date`` / ``removal_date`` for the as-of window (half-open ``[)`` semantics).  Note: ``cik`` is named ``cik`` here (NOT ``entity_id`` like security/filing/fact) so the JOIN with ``references`` uses the same column name on both sides — see migration 0015 for the rationale.

HISTORICAL DEPTH AND PROVENANCE DIFFER BY INDEX — read this before using the table for point-in-time work.  The ``source`` and ``confidence`` columns are the discriminators, and they are the ones to branch on.
* **SP500 — from 1996-01-02, ``high`` confidence.**  1,014 entry/exit spells over 968 CIKs, 510 of them closed, including companies long delisted, with ``removal_date`` and ``removal_reason`` populated.  ``source`` is ``historical_seed`` / ``public_constituent_list`` / ``succession_config``.
* **RUSSELL1000 / RUSSELL2000 / RUSSELL3000 — from 2000-09-30, ``medium`` confidence, ``source='fund_holdings'``.**  3,051 / 10,130 / 11,025 spells, of which 2,059 / 8,214 / 8,117 are closed.  Reconstructed from the publicly disclosed portfolio holdings of large funds tracking each index, NOT from the index provider's own constituent lists, which are licensed IP we do not redistribute.

Three bounds follow from that derivation and must be carried into any conclusion drawn from the Russell rows.  (1) OBSERVATION SPACING VARIES — roughly one to four observations a year from 2000 through 2006, monthly from 2007 on — so a join or leave date is only as precise as the interval between observations, and is never exact to the day in the early years.  (2) A tracking fund only PROXIES its index — a few holdings sit outside it and a sampled fund can miss members — so these are our derived membership, not the index.  (3) There is NO Russell data before 2000-09-30; an earlier date returns zero rows because we do not carry it, which is not a statement that the index was empty.  Confidence is therefore ``medium`` and never ``high``, which correctly leaves the MCP's ``pit_safe`` false.

MEASURED against the index provider's 13 published reconstitution lists (used to grade, never published): recall 96.5%–98.3% per year on RUSSELL3000, worst 96.5%.  Precision is 93.6%–98.6% once the official list's ~22-character truncated company names are accounted for; the unadjusted floor reads 87.3%–97.7% and understates early years, because a company renamed since the list date cannot be matched at all.

KNOWN GAP — no holdings observation exists anywhere between 2016-12-30 and 2017-07-31, a 213-day window, for any fund read.  Russell membership cannot be observed there, so departures collapse onto 2016-12-31 and arrivals onto 2017-07-31, and the June 2017 reconstitution therefore appears to happen on 31 July.  A year-end 2016 point-in-time query returns 2,623 RUSSELL3000 members rather than ~2,900 for this reason alone.  SP500 is unaffected.

SP500 pre-2007 coverage rises 1996 ≈341 members → 2006 ≈454 against a real ~500.  That shortfall is a CIK RESOLUTION ceiling, not the index's size: pre-XBRL delisted members were never ingested into ``entity``, and this table's ``cik`` is an FK to it.

index_name.description: Canonical short code.  Exactly four values are populated: SP500 | RUSSELL1000 | RUSSELL2000 | RUSSELL3000.  Depth and provenance differ per index — see the table description.

effective_date.description: First trading day the company traded as a member.

removal_date.description: First trading day the company was NOT a member.  NULL = current.  [) interval semantics — a company removed on 2017-06-19 is NOT a member on 2017-06-19.

removal_reason.description: merger | acquisition | bankruptcy | criteria | spinoff | other.  NULL when removal_date IS NULL.

successor_cik.description: Acquirer CIK when removal_reason in {merger, acquisition}. Essential for backtests crossing M&A — without it, a stock disappearing looks indistinguishable from a delisting.

source.description: Provenance — the column to branch on for how far a row can be trusted.  Every value names the MECHANISM that produced the row, never a firm or a website; that is a deliberate naming rule, so do not read a value as an attribution.  Live values with row counts (2026-09-17): ``fund_holdings`` 24,206 — publicly disclosed portfolio holdings of funds tracking each index, sole source of RUSSELL1000 / RUSSELL2000 / RUSSELL3000, always confidence='medium'; ``historical_seed`` 528 — curated S&P 500 spells 1996+; ``public_constituent_list`` 484 — current S&P 500 members, from a publicly maintained list of the index's constituents; ``succession_config`` 2 — curated reorg predecessor spells.  Valid but currently EMPTY: ``fund_snapshot``, ``manual``.  ⚠️ SUPERSEDED VALUES a cached older snapshot may still carry: earlier releases named the fund, list or publisher a row was read from instead of the mechanism.  Those values were renamed between 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-17 onto the mechanism names above — ``fund_holdings`` / ``fund_snapshot`` for the holdings-derived lanes, ``public_constituent_list`` for the current-members lane — and one belonged to a layer that was removed on 2026-09-17 having never written a row.  Treat any value not in the live list above as a stale snapshot, not as a fifth lane.

confidence.description: high | medium | low.  Drives get_pit_universe's ``pit_safe`` flag, which is true only when EVERY matched row is 'high'.  In practice: all RUSSELL rows are 'medium' (fund-derived, observed at varying intervals), so any Russell query is pit_safe=false by construction; curated S&P 500 spells are 'high', dropping to 'low' for pre-2001 dates where the seed is least certain.

first_seen_date.description: Panel metadata: the first date this constituent was actually OBSERVED in a holdings file.  Populated on every ``fund_holdings`` row (24,206), every ``public_constituent_list`` row (484) and 16 ``historical_seed`` rows; NULL on the rest of ``historical_seed`` and on ``succession_config``, which derive spells from a curated list rather than from an observed panel.  For a Russell row this is the honest observation window — ``effective_date`` may precede it only by the panel's observation granularity.

last_seen_date.description: Panel metadata — last date this constituent was observed in a holdings file.  Populated wherever ``first_seen_date`` is; NULL on the curated layers.

avg_weight_pct.description: Panel metadata — average index weight (%) over the observed window.  Populated on 18,658 of the 24,206 ``fund_holdings`` rows — the dated holdings files carry weights, the earlier SEC-filed schedules do not; NULL elsewhere, including ``public_constituent_list``, which carries no weights.

industry_classification.description: Point-in-time industry classification (SEC SIC): one row per company and SIC spell, built from the SIC each filer itself reported in its own filings (SEC filing header and SEC filing metadata). `valid_from` is the SEC acceptance instant of the first filing that showed the SIC; `valid_to` (exclusive) is where the next spell starts, NULL for the current one. There are no rows before a company's first evidence: history is never back-filled, so a backtest dated earlier must decide for itself (using the first spell is the nearest-in-time choice). A -> B -> A is three spells: a real reassignment is not smoothed. `references.sector` / `industry` / `sic_code` and `entity` are CURRENT values and are NOT point-in-time: use this table for as-of questions (`valid_from <= t AND (valid_to IS NULL OR t < valid_to)`). `sector` is the same SIC-to-sector mapping `references.sector` uses, applied to the spell's SIC. No GICS (licensed by MSCI and S&P): 4-digit SIC is the finest level published. Sliced like `references` (same companies per tier), no date window.

sic_description.description: SEC's published description of the code; the latest filer-reported text when the code is not on the SEC list.

sector.description: Sector of this SIC under the same mapping as references.sector.

industry.description: Filer-reported SIC description (the meaning of entity.industry).

valid_from.description: Acceptance instant of the first filing showing this SIC (see valid_from_basis).

valid_to.description: Exclusive end: the next spell's valid_from; NULL = current.

first_accession_id.description: Accession of the first filing in the spell (NULL if only observed).

last_accession_id.description: Accession of the last filing in the spell (NULL if only observed).

evidence_count.description: Evidence rows folded into the spell.

valid_from_basis.description: sec_acceptance (exact acceptance time) | filing_date_eod (filing date, end of day) | observed (date we saw it).

standard_concept.description: Valuein's curated gold-standard concept catalog (~292 rows) — the dictionary for the ``fact.standard_concept`` column.  Each row is one L1/L2 concept (Revenue, GrossProfit, LongTermDebt, …) with its statement/category, definition, default unit, and Bloomberg/FactSet field equivalents.  Distinct from ``taxonomy_guide`` (the ~11,966-row raw SEC us-gaap tag reference for the ``fact.concept`` column): join ``fact.standard_concept = standard_concept.standard_concept`` for the curated label, ``fact.concept = taxonomy_guide.standard_concept`` for the raw tag.  The 'Other' catch-all row is included.

level.description: L1 (top statement line) | L2 (sector-pack sub-line) | -- (the 'Other' catch-all).

statement_type.description: income | balance_sheet | cash_flow | comprehensive_income | supplemental | dei | notes | other.

category.description: Finer grouping within the statement (e.g. revenue, working_capital, equity).

unit_default.description: Canonical unit (USD | USD/share | shares | pct | …); NULL for non-numeric.

is_flow.description: TRUE for flow (period) measures, FALSE for stock (point-in-time) measures.

parent_concept.description: Parent in the L1→L2 hierarchy (NULL for L1 / 'Other').

sector_pack.description: Sector pack a L2 concept belongs to (banking, insurance, reit, …); NULL unless level='L2'.

bloomberg_equivalent.description: Closest Bloomberg field mnemonic, when one exists.

factset_equivalent.description: Closest FactSet field, when one exists.

gaap_ifrs_comparable.description: TRUE when the concept maps cleanly across US-GAAP and IFRS filers.

reviewed.description: Human-in-the-loop CPA sign-off flag.  TRUE = an accountant has verified this concept's canonical name, statement_type and rule; the concept is then LOCKED — the standardization coverage loop only ever creates NEW concepts, never mutates a reviewed one.  Curated catalog rows default TRUE; loop-generated provisional rows are FALSE.

reviewed_by.description: Who signed off (e.g. 'J. Smith, CPA'); NULL when not individually attributed.

reviewed_at.description: ISO date of the CPA sign-off; NULL when not individually attributed.

review_confidence.description: Concept-level trust score in [0, 1] — the catalog analogue of ``fact.confidence_score``.  1.0 = CPA-verified (reviewed=TRUE); 0.7 = provisional loop output pending review.  Filter ``review_confidence >= 1.0`` for the accountant-verified concept set.  Distinct from the per-fact *match* accuracy.

taxonomy_guide.description: SEC us-gaap taxonomy tag reference (one row per raw tag, synced yearly from the FASB taxonomy) — the dictionary for ``fact.concept``, joined on ``fact.concept = taxonomy_guide.standard_concept``.  Not the dictionary for ``fact.standard_concept``: that is the curated ``standard_concept`` table.

level.description: Not populated (always NULL) for the raw us-gaap tag reference; the L1/L2 tier lives in the ``standard_concept`` table.

statement_type.description: Not populated (NULL) for the raw us-gaap tag reference; statement placement lives in the ``standard_concept`` table.

is_active.description: Always TRUE today: rows from earlier taxonomy vintages are kept, not deactivated.

gaap_ifrs_comparable.description: Reserved; not populated by any writer (always FALSE).

ratio.description: Pipeline-computed financial ratios per entity per fiscal period. Derived from fact data.  Written append-on-restatement: each row's ``accepted_at`` is the PIT vintage = max(accepted_at) of the input facts that produced it, so a restated period (recomputed from a later-filed fact) is a NEW vintage row rather than an overwrite — mirroring fact.parquet.  Filter as-of with ``accepted_at <= as_of`` then take the latest vintage to avoid look-ahead bias.  No accession_id (ratios derive from multiple filings).  ``accepted_at`` is NULL for cross-sectional rank rows (``*_sector_pctile``) and any year whose source facts lacked an acceptance timestamp; ``computed_at`` tracks the latest computation within a vintage.

category.description: Groups ratios for filtering without scanning all ratio_name values. Values: profitability | per_share | liquidity | leverage | efficiency | forensic | growth | owner_earnings | valuation. ``valuation`` holds only OBSERVED or PARAMETER-FREE measures — the export-time price multiples (pe_ratio, pb_ratio, ev_ebitda, dividend_yield, market_cap) plus graham_number and ncav_per_share. It carries no intrinsic-value estimate: an intrinsic value depends on the caller's discount rate, terminal growth and horizon, so it is computed on demand (MCP ``compute_dcf``) and never published as a fact.

confidence_score.description: Entity-period data quality: average fact.confidence_score of the facts feeding this period. Filter Bloomberg-grade with >= 0.95. NULL for cross-sectional rank rows (e.g. *_sector_pctile).

fiscal_period.description: FY | Q1 | Q2 | Q3 | Q4 | TTM

accepted_at.description: PIT vintage — SEC acceptance timestamp of the latest input fact (max(accepted_at) of the year's facts).  The date this ratio first became knowable.  NULL for cross-sectional rank rows and un-timestamped years.  Filter ``accepted_at <= as_of`` for look-ahead-free backtests, mirroring fact.accepted_at.

ingested_at.description: DB insertion timestamp; use ``computed_at`` for ratio freshness.

restatement_events.description: Restatement Radar feed — one row per financial fact that a later filing materially changed (>0.5% swing from the originally-reported value), across the full 1993→present archive.  Derived in DuckDB from fact.parquet by reproducing the fact_lineage_summary matview's aggregation over every vintage (see data-pipeline/services/restatements.py). Each row carries the original ('as reported') value, the current ('restated') value, the signed delta, a deterministic severity bucket, both filings' accessions for one-click SEC lineage, and a per-company magnitude rank ('Nth largest revision in this company's history').  Public-fact table — served to ALL tiers unsliced (copy-whole), including the free guest/sample tier, so the public /radar surface always shows the complete feed. ``event_id`` is a content hash of the tuple grain (cik, standard_concept, period_end, fiscal_period, unit), stable across re-restatements → stable /radar/[id] URL.

event_id.description: SHA-256 hex of cik|concept|period_end|fiscal_period|unit. Content-addressed on the tuple GRAIN (not the restating accession) so a fact restated twice keeps one stable id. Hashed over the RAW XBRL tag: hashing the canonical name would collide two different facts (many tags map to one standard_concept) onto one id and one /radar/[id] URL.

concept.description: The RAW XBRL tag both filings used (e.g. 'Revenues'). This is the detection grain AND the evidence the diff is apples-to-apples: a reader can open both accessions and confirm the same tag carries two different numbers. Diffing on standard_concept instead would compare values that were never comparable — see schema note 2.23.0.

concept_label.description: As-reported label from the latest filing; falls back to standard_concept.

statement_type.description: income_statement | balance_sheet | cash_flow (from the latest vintage).

period_start.description: Start of the reporting WINDOW the restated fact covers — part of the detection grain since 2.25.0, and the reason one fact is no longer published as two.  Read straight from the XBRL context, so unlike `fiscal_period` it cannot disagree with itself across filings.  It also separates the one case fiscal_period existed to handle: a 3-month quarter and a 6-month YTD figure share a `period_end` but never a `period_start`.  NULL for instant (balance-sheet) facts, which have no duration.

period_end.description: End of the reporting period the restated fact covers.

fiscal_period.description: FY | Q1 | Q2 | Q3 | Q4 — a DISPLAY LABEL, carried from the latest filing.  It is deliberately NOT part of the grain: it is missing on some vintages and wrong on others (real data: one period_end arrived tagged Q1, Q2 AND Q3), and an unreliable value in a grain splits one fact into several.  Use period_start/period_end for identity; use this to render it.

delta_pct.description: Signed relative change: (current − first) / |first|. Positive = revised up.

version_count.description: Number of filings that reported this tuple (≥2 for a restatement).

last_filed_at.description: accepted_at of the restating filing — the event's detection time / feed ordering key.

restated_in_form.description: SEC form the RESTATING filing arrived in (10-K, 10-K/A, 10-Q, 10-Q/A, 20-F…). The single most important qualifier on an event: a 10-K/A is the company formally telling the SEC it got a number wrong; a routine next-year 10-K carrying a revised comparative is a re-file. Nullable — LEFT JOINed from filing, so an early vintage with no filing row still publishes.

restated_in_amendment.description: TRUE when the restating filing is an amendment (filing.is_amendment). The strongest signal a restatement is real and acknowledged, and the primary editorial filter for the public feed. FALSE when unknown — never claim an amendment we cannot prove.

first_primary_doc.description: Primary document of the AS-REPORTED filing (e.g. 'goog-20251231.htm').  Lets a consumer build SEC's inline-XBRL viewer URL — /ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/{cik}/{accn}/{doc} — which opens the actual statement with every tagged fact live and searchable, instead of dumping the reader on a filing-index directory listing.  NULL when the filing row is unknown; the link then degrades to the index page.

current_primary_doc.description: Primary document of the RESTATING filing.  See first_primary_doc — a diff has two sides and both should open on the page the number is actually printed on.

first_is_inline_xbrl.description: TRUE when the AS-REPORTED filing is Inline XBRL (filing.is_inline_xbrl, the SEC-declared flag).  TRUE → link SEC's viewer: https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/{cik}/{accn}/{doc}.  FALSE → link the document directly (/Archives/edgar/data/{cik}/{accn}/{doc}), or {accession}-index.htm when first_primary_doc is NULL or the filing predates 2001 — the /ix viewer renders nothing for a non-iXBRL document (≈2009–2019 classic XBRL and everything earlier).  Use this stored flag, never a date heuristic.  NOT NULL: FALSE when the filing row is unknown.

current_is_inline_xbrl.description: TRUE when the RESTATING filing is Inline XBRL.  Same link rules as first_is_inline_xbrl, applied to current_accession / current_primary_doc.  NOT NULL: FALSE when the filing row is unknown.

disclosure_class.description: HOW the company told the market — 'non_reliance' | 'amended' | 'undisclosed'.  'non_reliance': an 8-K carrying Item 4.02 ('Non-Reliance on Previously Issued Financial Statements') was filed between the original and the restating filing — the company formally telling the SEC not to rely on what it had already reported.  The loudest signal in US disclosure, and rare (6 companies in the whole S&P 500 slice).  'amended': corrected in a 10-K/A or 10-Q/A.  'undisclosed': the value changed inside a ROUTINE periodic filing — no 4.02, no amendment; the old number is simply gone.  94.5% of events are 'undisclosed', which is the whole point of the column.  NOT NULL (defaults to 'undisclosed'): a missing disclosure is exactly what 'undisclosed' means, so there is no third state.  ⚠ It is NOT named 'silent' on purpose — see the 2.24.0 note at the top of this file.  It is a statement about the filing chain, not about the filer's intent.

severity.description: Deterministic magnitude bucket: high (|Δ|≥10%) | medium (≥2%) | low (≥0.5%).

concept_importance.description: How much an analyst cares that THIS line moved: 1 headline (revenue, net income, EPS, total assets, operating cash flow), 2 primary statement line, 3 footnote (lease schedules, share counts, tax-rate reconciliations). Drives company_rank, so a revenue restatement outranks a footnote that happened to swing further.

company_rank.description: Rank of this event within the company's restatement history (1 = most significant). Ordered by concept_importance FIRST, then |delta_pct|, then period_end — so a revenue restatement outranks a lease-schedule footnote that swung further. The feed keeps each company's top 10 (see FEED_TOP_N_PER_COMPANY: the full detection is ~1M rows, which OOMs the 128MB MCP Worker when read whole).

stock_price.description: Coarse end-of-day market-price series per entity — period-end-aligned closes (one per fiscal period_end, for value-vs-price overlays) AND a monthly last-trading-day close history (for charting/backtest scaffolding).  Filter on ``observation`` to pick the grain.  RAW closes (never split/dividend-adjusted — split-invariant ratios need no adjustment); ``div_cash`` / ``split_factor`` carry the corporate-action factors for query-time total-return adjustment.  Point-in-time: ``accepted_at`` = the market-close timestamp, so an ``as_of`` before the close never sees that bar. GRAIN: one row per (entity_id, observation, period_end-or-month) — this table is joined to per-CIK fundamentals, so an issuer with several listed securities is resolved to its PRIMARY listing before alignment; ``security_id`` / ``symbol`` record which one, so a P/E is auditable back to the share class it was computed from.  ``total_return_index`` (3.3.0) is that listing's daily total-return index sampled at these closes, so the ratio of two month-end rows is the total return between them — dividends between the two month-ends included — and a monthly-rebalanced backtest needs nothing finer.  Every tier carries this table.  For every listing of a multi-class issuer, and for daily bars, read ``stock_price_daily`` — Institutional and Pro only.  Derived at export from the internal licensed price archive.  ⚠️ COVERAGE FLOOR: licensed market data, NOT EDGAR — it does NOT start at EDGAR's 1993 floor.  No bars exist in 1993; the earliest bar differs per security and is 1994 or later (measured 2026-09-12).

security_id.description: The listing this close came from — the issuer's primary ticker where SEC flags one, else its deepest-traded listing.  Added 2.29.0; before it, which share class priced a multi-class issuer was arbitrary.

symbol.description: Ticker of ``security_id``, denormalized so no join is needed to read it.

price_date.description: Trading day the close is from.

split_factor.description: Split factor on price_date (1.0 if none).

accepted_at.description: Market-close PIT stamp for price_date; filter ``accepted_at <= as_of``.

period_end.description: Fiscal period this close aligns to (observation='period_end'); NULL for monthly rows.

observation.description: 'period_end' (close at/just-before a fiscal close) | 'monthly' (last trading day of a month).

total_return_index.description: The priced listing's total-return index at this close — the same series as ``stock_price_daily.total_return_index`` (forward-compounded from the listing's first archived bar, arbitrary base ≈ 1.0, dividends reinvested, splits neutralized, PIT-immutable), sampled at the coarse grain.  Only RATIOS are meaningful: ``tri_b / tri_a - 1`` between two ``monthly`` rows is the holder's total return for that span, INCLUDING every dividend whose ex-date fell between them — which ``div_cash`` on a month-end row cannot tell you, because it names only that day's dividend.  NULL only where the daily index is NULL for the listing.  Added 3.3.0.

stock_price_daily.description: Daily OHLCV bar series — one row per (SECURITY, trading day), NOT downsampled (unlike the coarse ``stock_price`` table).  Powers as-of-arbitrary-date price lookups (latest close on-or-before any calendar date) and total-return backtests.  ⚠️ GRAIN IS PER SECURITY, NOT PER COMPANY: an issuer with several listed securities (GOOG + GOOGL, a tracking stock, a contingent value right) contributes one row per listing, and both are real prices.  Partition or filter on ``security_id`` — a window function partitioned on ``entity_id`` alone alternates between two unrelated price series.  For one row per company per day, add ``WHERE is_primary_listing``.  TOTAL RETURN: use ``total_return_index``, not ``adjusted_close`` (which carries NO history before 2026-06-29, so it truncates a backtest instead of failing it) and never raw ``close`` (which drops ~75% on a 4-for-1 split).  Point-in-time: ``accepted_at`` = the market-close timestamp, so an ``as_of`` filter before the close never sees that bar.  Derived at export time from the internal licensed price archive via the same date-aware ticker→CIK resolution as ``stock_price``.  ⚠️ INSTITUTIONAL AND PRO ONLY (since 3.3.0, 2026-09-17): sliced + per-CIK partitioned for full (all history) and pro (15y); NOT published to the free tiers, whose manifests do not list it.  The archive is licensed market data on terms that cover derived measures, not redistribution of the series, and the free tiers are read without a contract.  On those tiers use the coarse ``stock_price`` table (period-end + month-end closes with ``total_return_index``), and the valuation multiples in ``ratio``.  ⚠️ COVERAGE FLOOR: this is licensed market data, NOT EDGAR, so it does NOT start at EDGAR's 1993 floor.  No bars exist in 1993; the earliest bar differs per security and is 1994 or later (measured against production 2026-09-12).  A range before a security's first bar returns no rows on EVERY tier, Institutional included — that is data coverage, not a plan limit.

security_id.description: The listing this bar belongs to.  ``(security_id, price_date)`` is the table's unique key — ``(entity_id, price_date)`` is NOT.  Added 2.29.0.

symbol.description: Ticker of ``security_id``, denormalized so no join is needed to read it.

is_primary_listing.description: TRUE on exactly one bar per (entity_id, price_date): the issuer's representative listing.  Decided by SEC's primary-ticker flag, falling back to the deepest-traded listing, with the ticker breaking any remaining tie.  Filter on it to get one row per company per day without a join to ``security``.

price_date.description: Trading day the bar is from.

adjusted_close.description: ⚠️ DO NOT BACKTEST ON THIS COLUMN — use ``total_return_index``.  It is not sparse, it is TRUNCATED: measured over 136,728 bars of ten large caps (2026-09-12) it is populated on 100% of bars from 2026-06-29 onward and on 0% of every bar before, because the column was added in schema 2.20.0 and older archive files are backfilled all-null.  So ``WHERE adjusted_close IS NOT NULL`` does not sample history — it silently cuts a 60-year series down to the most recent few weeks and returns a result with no error.  ``total_return_index`` is derived from ``close`` / ``div_cash`` / ``split_factor``, which are complete, and is PIT-immutable; this column is back-adjusted, so every later corporate action retroactively rewrites it and a backtest run last year no longer reproduces.  Kept only because where it IS present it is the vendor's own series and agrees with ours to r = 0.9999937.

total_return_index.description: Total-return index for this listing, forward-compounded from its first bar in the archive (arbitrary base ≈ 1.0 — only RATIOS of it are meaningful).  Reinvests dividends and neutralizes splits: ``tri_b / tri_a - 1`` is the return a holder actually earned between two dates.  Built from ``close``/``div_cash``/``split_factor``, all of which are 100% populated, using the vendor's multiplicative convention ``close_t * split_t / (close_t-1 - div_t)``.  PIT-IMMUTABLE, unlike a back-adjusted price series: tomorrow's dividend appends a new value rather than rewriting today's, so a backtest run last year still reproduces.  Compounds per SECURITY — a ticker RENAME starts a new series, because the price archive is keyed on ticker and genuinely has no bar linking the two.

split_factor.description: Split factor on price_date (1.0 if none).

accepted_at.description: Market-close PIT stamp for price_date; filter ``accepted_at <= as_of``.

insider_party.description: Directory of every insider / reporting person referenced by Form 3/4/5/144.  Keyed on CIK when SEC-registered, otherwise on a normalized name.  Joined to insider_transaction via insider_party_id.  FULL bucket only — enterprise tier (full plan).

cik.description: 10-digit zero-padded SEC CIK; NULL for filers without an SEC-registered identity (rare individual reporters).

normalized_name.description: Uppercased + whitespace-collapsed name for CIK-less filer dedup.

insider_filing.description: Form 3 / 4 / 5 / SC 13D / SC 13G / 144 (and amendments) — the subject-rooted insider DISCLOSURE filing record.  Distinct from ``filing`` (financial-statement forms) so the financial table stays clean.  ``subject_cik`` is the issuer the disclosure is about — a SOFT reference (LEFT JOIN to entity.cik when in the fundamentals universe; may be NULL/unmatched for foreign / pre-IPO / delisted issuers).  ``filer_party_id`` FKs to ``insider_party`` (the insider / holder).  Children ``insider_transaction`` and ``insider_ownership`` FK to this table via accession_id.  FULL bucket only — enterprise tier.

accession_id.description: Unique SEC accession ID for this disclosure filing.

subject_cik.description: Issuer CIK the disclosure is about — soft reference (LEFT JOIN to entity.cik; no hard FK).

filer_party_id.description: FK to the insider / holder in insider_party (NULL when unresolved).

filer_cik.description: Denormalised filer CIK for query convenience.

superseded_by.description: Accession of the AMENDMENT (3/A, 4/A, 5/A) that replaces this filing, the next link in the chain; NULL on the latest version.  Matched by reporting owner + issuer + earliest transaction date (Form 3: owner + issuer) and ONLY when exactly one original fits: an ambiguous or unmatched amendment stays NULL.  Drop superseded filings (and their insider_transaction rows) with ``superseded_by IS NULL`` to avoid counting a corrected trade twice.  Forms 3/4/5 /A: owner + issuer + original filing date, else + earliest transaction date.  Form 144/A: the explicit previous accession, else filer + issuer + approximate sale date.  SC 13D/G (filing grain): the same primary reporting person's next SC 13D/G on the same subject (original or amendment, either schedule); see ``insider_ownership.superseded_by`` for positions.

accepted_at_precision.description: 'exact' | 'date_only'.  'date_only' means accepted_at is 22:00 America/New_York of filing_date (an upper bound).

source_format.description: How the row was extracted: xml | dataset | html | text.  NULL = ingested before 2026-10.

original_filing_date.description: Forms 3/4/5 /A: dateOfOriginalSubmission, the filing date of the amended filing.

amends_accession_id.description: Explicit pointer filed by the amendment (Form 144/A and SC 13D/G XML previousAccessionNumber). Soft reference: the amended filing may not be in this table.

is_rule_10b5_1.description: Form 4/5 Rule 10b5-1 checkbox (schema 2023-04+).  NULL = the form version has no checkbox.

plan_adoption_date.description: Form 144 planAdoptionDates.  NULL = none filed, or several distinct dates.

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the superseded_by filing, the instant this filing stops being current.  NULL while it is the latest version.  Filter ``superseded_at IS NULL OR superseded_at > :as_of`` for a point-in-time view.

insider_transaction.description: Form 3 / 4 / 5 / 144 line items — each row is one transaction, initial holding, or proposed sale by an insider.  transaction_type is 'transaction' (Form 4/5), 'initial_holding' (Form 3), or 'proposed_sale' (Form 144).  Joins to ``insider_filing`` via accession_id, to ``entity`` (issuer) via entity_id (soft ref), and to ``insider_party`` via insider_party_id.  FULL bucket only.

entity_id.description: Issuer CIK (the company whose securities the insider holds).  Soft reference — LEFT JOIN to entity.cik when the issuer is in the fundamentals universe; may not resolve for foreign / pre-IPO / delisted issuers.

transaction_type.description: transaction | initial_holding | proposed_sale.  (holding and reported_sale arrive with 5.0.0; they are not published yet.)  Flow aggregates use transaction_type = 'transaction'.

price_per_share.description: Price per share as filed, in dollars.  NULL when the filed value is above $1,000,000 per share, which is an aggregate dollar amount typed into the per-share field (for example AMD 2017-08-04: 525,600,000 for 40,000,000 shares); shares and the filing itself are unchanged, so the dollar total stays derivable from the filing.

aggregate_market_value.description: Form 144 only — proposed-sale total dollar value.

accepted_at.description: The parent filing's SEC acceptance instant (UTC), joined from insider_filing at export.

insider_name.description: DENORMALIZED from insider_party.name (LEFT JOIN on insider_party_id at export). Inlined so the MCP Worker resolves the reporting insider's name from this tiny per-CIK partition without decoding the 406K-row insider_party dimension (the CF 1102 OOM). NULL if the party_id has no dimension match.

acquired_disposed_code.description: A | D as filed (transactionAcquiredDisposedCode): the only unambiguous sign for codes J/G/M/C/X.  NULL on holdings, Form 3 and Form 144 rows.

conversion_or_exercise_price.description: Table II derivative conversion or exercise price as filed.  NULL when the box holds only a footnote reference.

exercise_date.description: Table II date exercisable.  NULL when footnote-only.

expiration_date.description: Table II expiration date.  NULL when footnote-only.

footnote_refs.description: Footnote references of this line, one '<column>:<footnote_id>' token each ('price_per_share:F1', 'row:F3').  Resolve against insider_footnote.  NULL = none.

accepted_at_precision.description: DERIVED from the parent filing: 'exact' | 'date_only' (accepted_at is then 22:00 America/New_York of the filing date, an upper bound).

is_amendment.description: DERIVED: the parent filing is a /A.

superseded_by.description: DERIVED: accession of the amendment that replaces this row's filing; NULL when current.

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the superseding filing.  A row is current as of D when accepted_at <= D AND (superseded_at IS NULL OR superseded_at > D).

is_rule_10b5_1.description: DERIVED from the parent filing's Rule 10b5-1 checkbox (Forms 4/5, 2023-04+).

institutional_filing.description: Form 13F-HR / 13F-NT (and amendments) — the manager-rooted filing record.  Distinct from ``filing`` (issuer-rooted) because 13F filings have no single subject issuer (the manager reports a portfolio across many issuers).  FK to ``insider_party`` for the manager.  FULL bucket only — enterprise tier.

accession_id.description: Unique SEC accession ID for this 13F filing.

filer_party_id.description: FK to the manager's row in insider_party.

filer_cik.description: Denormalised manager CIK — mirrors institutional_holding.filer_cik for query convenience.

amendment_no.description: The cover page's amendment number (0 on an original).

superseded_by.description: Accession of the 13F-HR/A RESTATEMENT that replaces this filing (the first restatement filed after it for the same manager and period); NULL on the latest version.  A NEW HOLDINGS amendment only adds positions: it supersedes nothing and stays live beside its original.  A manager's book for a period is the holdings of the filings with ``superseded_by IS NULL`` (summing every filing double counts a restated report).

source_format.description: xml | dataset | text.  NULL = ingested before 2026-10.

report_type.description: 13F HOLDINGS REPORT | 13F NOTICE | 13F COMBINATION REPORT (cover page).

amendment_type.description: RESTATEMENT | NEW HOLDINGS on an amendment; NULL on an original or when unreadable.

table_entry_total.description: Summary page: number of information-table entries.

value_total_usd.description: Summary page: value total, in WHOLE dollars (scaled by value_units like institutional_holding.market_value_usd).

value_units.description: Units of every VALUE in this filing as filed: thousands | dollars.  The export scales to whole dollars from this verdict.  NULL on a notice (13F-NT) and on filings not yet classified (the export then falls back to the filing date).

filer_crd_number.description: The manager's FINRA/IARD CRD number (1-12 digits), as filed on the 13F cover.  Joins to investment_adviser.crd_number (Form ADV, also FULL tier) to link a 13F manager to its adviser record.  NULL when not stated.  A public registration number, not a security identifier.

form13f_file_number.description: The manager's Form 13F file number (028-NNNNN), as filed.  NULL when not stated.

reconciliation_status.description: Text-era filings: reconciled | unreconciled | no_totals (the filing's own totals check).  Holdings rows are published only for reconciled filings.

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the superseded_by filing; NULL while current.

institutional_holding.description: Form 13F-HR holdings — institutional managers' quarterly position disclosures.  One row per filed information-table line (``holding_line_no``): a filing may list one security on several lines (per investment discretion or other manager), and the position is their sum.  ``shares_or_principal_type = 'PRN'`` rows are bonds / convertible notes whose ``shares`` is a face amount in dollars: filter ``shares_or_principal_type = 'SH'`` before summing shares.  Joins to ``institutional_filing`` via accession_id (the 13F filing record); ``filer_cik`` is the manager CIK (denormalised — same value as institutional_filing.filer_cik). ``subject_entity_id`` is the issuer CIK (NULL until the internal issuer resolution succeeds).  FULL bucket only — enterprise tier.

filer_cik.description: Manager CIK (denormalised from institutional_filing.filer_cik for query convenience). BY DESIGN this does NOT resolve against ``entity`` for most filers (measured 2026-09-22: 296 of 13,229 distinct filer CIKs, 2.2%) — a 13F filer is the MONEY MANAGER (an investment adviser required to file because it exercises >= $100M discretionary AUM), not an SEC-registered company issuer, so its CIK is drawn from the same namespace as ``entity`` but is rarely a member of it. Since the 2026-05-14 filer redesign, filer identity (name, cik) lives in ``insider_party`` (``party_type='entity'``, ``JOIN insider_party ON insider_party.cik = institutional_holding.filer_cik``) rather than in ``entity`` — entity is deliberately kept scoped to the issuer/fundamentals universe. Do not treat a filer_cik orphan against ``entity`` as a data-quality defect.

filer_name.description: DENORMALIZED 13F manager name (LEFT JOIN insider_party on filer_cik = cik at export time). Lets consumers render the holder name without decoding the insider_party dimension. NULL only when the manager CIK is unresolved.

share_class_figi.description: OpenFIGI share-class FIGI (12 characters, e.g. BBG001S5N8V8) of the security held; joins directly to ``references.share_class_figi`` / ``security.share_class_figi``.  Replaces the CUSIP, which Valuein does not publish.  NULL when the security has no share-class FIGI (debt, munis, notes), when the mapping is ambiguous, or when OpenFIGI does not know the security (about 15% of all-history rows, about 2-4% of recent ones).  Option rows carry the underlying security's FIGI; ``put_call`` disambiguates.

subject_entity_id.description: Resolved issuer CIK; NULL until Valuein's issuer resolution step maps the holding to a company. A genuine share of NULLs is expected (options/derivatives, ETFs and funds-of-funds, foreign issuers outside the ``entity`` universe — none of these have a company CIK to resolve to). Separately, until 2026-09-22 the backfill's own SELECT was unbounded (one ``fetch()`` over the whole NULL set) and OOM-killed the resolve phase on every scheduled run for >= 5 consecutive weeks (2026-08-16 → 2026-09-13) before resolving a single row — see the issuer-resolver module for the fix (keyset-paginated by id). Coverage should climb from its 2026-09-22 baseline (65.7% NULL) once the paginated backfill actually completes on a live run; a coverage figure quoted before that run should not be read as the resolver's ceiling.

market_value_usd.description: Position value in WHOLE US dollars, as published.  Filers reported 13F VALUE in thousands of dollars before 2023-01-03 (and a minority for months after); the export multiplies the filings whose institutional_filing.value_units is 'thousands' by 1,000 (a filing without a verdict falls back to its filing date; domain/thirteenf_units.py), so this column is always whole dollars.

put_call.description: PUT | CALL | NULL (NULL = common stock, not an option).

investment_discretion.description: SOLE | DFND | OTR (Form 13F bulk vocabulary) or SOLE | SHARED | NONE (per-filing XML vocabulary).

accepted_at.description: The parent 13F filing's SEC acceptance instant (UTC), joined from institutional_filing at export.

shares_or_principal_type.description: SH = shares | PRN = principal amount in dollars (then ``shares`` holds the principal as filed: a face amount, not a share count).  PRN rows are published from 4.4.0; filter ``shares_or_principal_type = 'SH'`` before summing shares.

other_managers.description: Sequence numbers this line cites from the filing's 'Other Included Managers' list (institutional_other_manager, list_kind = 'included'), normalised '1,2,4'.  NULL = none.

holding_line_no.description: The filing's own line sequence, 1-based: the filed XML information table's document order (canonical); SEC's data-set INFOTABLE_SK rank only for a filing whose XML is not held.  One source per filing.  (accession_id, holding_line_no) identifies the row.  NULL on rows stored before 2026-10, whose line order was not kept.

is_amendment.description: DERIVED: the parent filing is a 13F-HR/A.

superseded_by.description: DERIVED: accession of the 13F-HR/A RESTATEMENT that replaces this row's filing; NULL when current.

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the superseding restatement.  A book as of D is the rows with accepted_at <= D AND (superseded_at IS NULL OR superseded_at > D).

insider_ownership.description: SC 13D / SC 13G beneficial-ownership disclosures (5%+ stakes).  One row per (filing, reporting person).  Group filings carry multiple reporting persons — each lands as a separate row.  Joins to ``insider_filing`` via accession_id; subject_entity_id is the issuer CIK (the company being held — soft ref, LEFT JOIN to entity).  FULL bucket only — enterprise tier (full plan).

filer_cik.description: Reporting-person CIK; NULL when not SEC-registered (many institutional disclosures only carry a name).

filer_party_id.description: FK into ``insider_party`` for the reporting person.  Resolved at merge time from the cover-page filer name via normalized_name match.  Use this column for cross-filing roll-ups ("every disclosure by this filer over time"); ``filer_name`` stays as the verbatim cover-page text for display.

subject_entity_id.description: Issuer CIK — the company whose stock is held.  Soft reference — LEFT JOIN to entity.cik when in the fundamentals universe.

schedule_type.description: SC 13D | SC 13D/A | SC 13G | SC 13G/A (or SCHEDULE 13… long-form variants — both vocabularies accepted).

accepted_at.description: The parent filing's SEC acceptance instant (UTC), joined from insider_filing at export.

superseded_by.description: Accession of the SAME reporting person's next SC 13D/G on the same subject (original or amendment, either schedule, in (accepted_at, accession_id) order); NULL on that person's latest filing.  Use this grain for positions: a group filing that drops a member leaves that member's last row current until the member files again.

reporting_person_type.description: Cover 'Type of Reporting Person' codes as filed (BD, BK, IC, IV, IA, EP, HC, SA, CP, CO, PN, IN, FI, OO); multi-valued.

is_amendment.description: DERIVED: the parent filing is an SC 13D/A or 13G/A.

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the superseded_by filing; NULL while current.

insider_footnote.description: Form 3 / 4 / 5 footnotes — the receipt behind a 10b5-1 plan, a weighted-average price or a plan adoption date, which the extraction never parses out of the text.  Lines cite them through ``insider_transaction.footnote_refs``.  Joins to ``insider_filing`` via accession_id.  FULL bucket only; monolithic parquet only (no per-CIK partitions).

footnote_text.description: Verbatim footnote text; security identifiers redacted.

is_truncated.description: TRUE when the source capped the text (the SEC data set caps at 1,023 characters).

accepted_at.description: DERIVED: the parent filing's SEC acceptance instant (UTC).

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the amendment that replaces the parent filing; NULL while current.

institutional_other_manager.description: 13F manager lists.  list_kind 'included' = the summary page's 'List of Other Included Managers' (numbered; cited by ``institutional_holding.other_managers``); 'reporting_for' = the cover page's 'Other Managers Reporting for this Manager'.  Public SEC / FINRA numbers only.  Joins to ``institutional_filing`` via accession_id.  FULL bucket only; monolithic parquet only.

ordinal.description: 1-based position in the list as filed.

name.description: Manager name as filed; security identifiers redacted.

accepted_at.description: DERIVED: the parent filing's SEC acceptance instant (UTC).

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the restatement that replaces the parent filing; NULL while current.

insider_ownership_purpose.description: Schedule 13D Item 4 'Purpose of Transaction', verbatim: raw filed text only, no summary and no classification.  13D / 13D/A only (13G has no Item 4); an amendment that does not restate Item 4 has NO row (never carried forward).  Joins to ``insider_filing`` via accession_id.  FULL bucket only; monolithic parquet only.

subject_cik.description: Issuer CIK whose shares the 13D concerns.

purpose_text.description: Whitespace-normalised Item 4 text, capped at 100,000 characters; security identifiers redacted.

char_count.description: Length of the full item before the cap.

is_truncated.description: TRUE when char_count exceeds the published text.

accepted_at.description: DERIVED: the parent filing's SEC acceptance instant (UTC).

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the filing that replaces the parent; NULL while current.

investment_adviser.description:
SEC Form ADV Part 1A — registered investment advisers and Exempt Reporting Advisers (~23.6K firms).  A SEPARATE SEC SOURCE from EDGAR: advisers file into IARD (operated by FINRA Regulation), so rows key on the firm's CRD number, NOT a CIK.  Sourced from the daily IAPD bulk feed ``IA_FIRM_SEC_Feed_*.xml.gz``.

PIT: the natural key is (crd_number, filing_date) where filing_date is the adviser's own Form ADV filing date.  A firm's annual updating amendment APPENDS a new vintage instead of overwriting the prior one — the same append-on-restatement shape as ``ratio.accepted_at``.  Filter ``filing_date <= as_of`` and take the latest vintage per crd_number for a point-in-time view, or the whole partition for adviser history.

⚠ Items 5.A–5.F are ABSENT for firm_type='ERA' — Exempt Reporting Advisers file an abbreviated form.  That is a different filing obligation, NOT missing data; scope coverage metrics to firm_type='Registered' or you understate completeness by ~28%.

FULL (Institutional) bucket only.

crd_number.description: IARD firm identifier (Item 1.E.(1)) — the natural key. Not a CIK.

filing_date.description: PIT vintage — the date the adviser filed this Form ADV.

sec_region.description: SEC regional office code, e.g. NYRO.

umbrella_registration.description: Filing covers a group of relying advisers under one umbrella registration.

cik.description: SOFT link the adviser self-disclosed to EDGAR (Item 1.D.(3)).  NULL for most advisers — so a NULL is expected, not an error.  Populated only from the monthly FOIA bundles, which are a filing-event stream needing ~12 months to converge on the full ~23.6K-adviser population; only 2 months have ever been ingested, so the measured population rate is ~4.55% (1,075 of 23,602 as of 2026-09-22) — the ``~26% of filers`` figure elsewhere describes the CIK CSV member's disclosure share WITHIN one monthly bundle, not the share of ``investment_adviser`` rows carrying a CIK; do not conflate the two.  ⚠️ Even where populated this rarely resolves to ``entity``: most self-disclosed CIKs belong to SEC filers with no public ticker (broker-dealer subsidiaries, holding entities) that fall outside the ``entity`` table's tickered-issuer scope — measured 6 of 1,075 (0.56%) actually join.  This is a real but rare bridge from an adviser to entity / institutional_holding, not a guaranteed one.

firm_type.description: 'Registered' (SEC-registered adviser) | 'ERA' (Exempt Reporting Adviser). ERAs file an abbreviated Form ADV — Items 5.A–5.F are NULL for them.

feed_generated_on.description: Date the IAPD bulk snapshot was generated (feed freshness).

employees_advisory_research.description: Item 5.B.(1) — employees who perform investment advisory functions INCLUDING RESEARCH.  The in-house research-capacity measure; NULL for ERAs.

employees_registered_reps.description: Item 5.B.(2) — registered representatives of a broker-dealer.

clients_without_raum.description: Item 5.C.(1) — clients for whom the adviser reports NO regulatory AUM.

pct_clients_non_us.description: Item 5.C.(2) — percent of clients who are non-US persons (0-100).

client_type_counts.description: Item 5.D client counts keyed by category: individuals, hnw_individuals, banking_thrift, investment_companies, business_development_companies, pooled_investment_vehicles, pension_profit_sharing, charitable_organizations, government_entities, other_investment_advisers, insurance_companies, sovereign_wealth_funds, corporations, other.  Absent key = not reported.

client_type_raum.description: Item 5.D regulatory AUM by the same category keys as client_type_counts. VERIFIED IDENTITY: these values sum EXACTLY to raum_total (checked at ingest across every adviser reporting both — 100% agreement).

reports_raum.description: Item 5.F.(1) — does the adviser report RAUM.

raum_total.description:
Item 5.F.(2)(c) — total regulatory assets under management (USD).
⚠ STRUCTURALLY DOUBLE-COUNTED across sub-advisory and affiliated-adviser relationships: the same dollars are reported by every adviser in the chain, so summing this column across firms yields ~$177T, far above global AUM. Valid per-firm and for ranking/screening; NEVER aggregate it.

advisory_activities.description: Item 5.G.(1)-(12) service-type booleans: financial_planning, portfolio_mgmt_individuals, portfolio_mgmt_investment_companies, portfolio_mgmt_pooled_vehicles, portfolio_mgmt_businesses, pension_consulting, selection_of_other_advisers, publication_of_periodicals, security_ratings_or_pricing, market_timing_services, educational_seminars, other.

financial_planning_clients.description: Item 5.H — financial-planning client count, published by the SEC as a BUCKET string ('0', '1-10', '11-25', '26-50', '51-100', '101-250', '251-500', 'More than 500'), NOT an integer.  Stored verbatim; do not cast to a number.

affiliations.description: Item 7.A.(1)-(16) financial-industry affiliation booleans: broker_dealer, registered_rep_of_broker_dealer, commodity_pool_operator_or_cta, futures_commission_merchant, real_estate_broker_or_agent, insurance_company_or_agency, pension_consultant, trust_company, registered_municipal_advisor, registered_sb_swap_dealer, major_sb_swap_participant, accountant_or_accounting_firm, lawyer_or_law_firm, banking_or_thrift_institution, sponsor_or_syndicator_of_lps, other_investment_adviser_or_financial_planner.

has_private_funds.description: Item 7.B flag — does the adviser advise any private fund.  Fund-level detail lives in investment_adviser_private_fund, which is sourced from a DIFFERENT file; a TRUE here with no child rows means that adviser's Schedule D has not been ingested yet, not that the fund detail is missing from the SEC.

investment_adviser_private_fund.description:
Form ADV Schedule D, Section 7.B.(1) — private funds advised by a registered investment adviser.  One row per (adviser, fund, filing vintage); joins to ``investment_adviser`` on crd_number.

⚠ SOURCE + COVERAGE: the daily IAPD feed carries only the Item 7.B yes/no flag, so fund detail comes from the MONTHLY FOIA bundles (``ADV_Filing_Data_YYYYMMDD_YYYYMMDD.zip``), which are a FILING-EVENT stream — roughly 2.9K of 23.6K advisers per month.  Because each adviser files one annual updating amendment, coverage converges on the full fund-reporting population only across ~12 monthly bundles.  A partial load looks complete but is not: check ``investment_adviser.has_private_funds`` for the authoritative population count.

FULL (Institutional) bucket only.

crd_number.description: Advising firm's CRD number (soft ref — the parent is vintage-keyed).

fund_id.description: SEC private-fund identifier, e.g. '805-4964869201'. Stable across filings.

filing_date.description: PIT vintage — filing date of the reporting ADV.

filing_id.description: IARD FilingID the row was parsed from.

reference_id.description: Per-filing fund sequence id; join key to the Schedule D sub-files.

fund_type.description: Hedge Fund | Private Equity Fund | Real Estate Fund | Venture Capital Fund | Liquidity Fund | Securitized Asset Fund | Other Private Fund.

gross_asset_value.description: Fund gross asset value in USD (Schedule D 7.B.(1)(A)(11)).  Unlike the adviser RAUM column this is fund-level and NOT double-counted across advisers, except for master/feeder pairs — filter is_feeder_fund to avoid counting a feeder's assets alongside its master's.

exclusion_3c1.description: Relies on the Investment Company Act §3(c)(1) exclusion (≤100 holders).

exclusion_3c7.description: Relies on the §3(c)(7) exclusion (qualified purchasers only).

is_feeder_fund.description: TRUE = feeder in a master-feeder structure; exclude when summing GAV.

has_annual_audit.description: Fund is subject to an annual audit.

is_gaap.description: Financial statements prepared under US GAAP.

unqualified_opinion.description: Most recent audit produced an unqualified opinion.

uses_prime_broker.description: Fund uses a prime broker.  A PRESENCE flag — the SEC reports Y/N here, not a name.

auditor_name.description: Auditing firm name, resolved from Schedule D 7.B.(1)(A)(23).

auditor_pcaob_registered.description: Auditor is registered with the PCAOB (7.B.(1)(A)(23)).
